endpoints.summary: Returns templates filtered by Contract Type, Industry and/or Status; used both by Template Library listing and New Contract template selection
Creates a new template as Version 1; transitions to Active once mandatory fields are complete
Edits an existing template, creating a new version entry recording editor and timestamp; blocks concurrent conflicting saves
Deactivates a template; blocked if attached to any active, unsigned contract
Reactivates an Inactive template with no restrictions
Returns the version history of a template including version number, editor and change summary

tables.name: templates
tables.description: Stores current state of templates used for contract generation

tables.name: template_versions
tables.description: Stores immutable snapshots of each saved template version with editor and timestamp

stories.title: Prompt Upload of Third Party Paper When No Active Templates Exist
stories.story_statement: As a Contract Owner, I want to be prompted to upload third party paper when no active templates exist for my selected Contract Type/Industry combination, so that I can still proceed with contract creation without being blocked by missing templates.
acceptance_criteria: Given I am on the New Contract Creation screen, when I select a Contract Type and Industry combination for which no active templates exist, then the system displays the message 'No active templates available for this combination. Please upload third party paper.' and disables the Template dropdown.

Given the system has displayed the no-active-templates message, when I proceed to complete the contract, then I must use the Upload Third Party Paper option instead of selecting a Template, and the Template field remains unavailable.

Given the no-active-templates message is displayed, when I continue entering contract details, then I must still be able to populate all remaining required data points: Contract Type, Industry, Counterparty Search, Counterparty Name, Counterparty Email, Counterparty Company, Counterparty Address, Counterparty GST/Tax ID, Contract Owner, Contract Value, Currency, Start Date, End Date, Renewal Type, Notice Period, Assigned Date, and Due Date.

Given I have uploaded a third party paper after seeing the no-active-templates message, when I attempt to also select a Template, then the system prevents this because Template and Upload Third Party Paper remain mutually exclusive.
Given no active template exists and I have not uploaded third party paper, when I attempt to Save the contract, then the system blocks the save until a third party paper is uploaded.

stories.title: Filter Template Dropdown by Active Status, Contract Type, and Industry
stories.story_statement: As a Contract Owner, I want to see only Active templates filtered by the selected Contract Type and Industry in the Template dropdown, so that I can quickly select a valid, approved template for my new contract.
stories.notes_assumptions: The fourth acceptance criterion enumerates all 18 required data points as context fields present on the New Contract Creation screen per the extraction requirement, though BR-1 itself specifically governs only the Template, Contract Type, and Industry fields.
acceptance_criteria: Given I am on the New Contract Creation screen and have selected a Contract Type and an Industry, When the Template dropdown is populated, Then it displays only templates with status = Active that match both the selected Contract Type and Industry.
Given a template has status other than Active for the selected Contract Type and Industry combination, When I open the Template dropdown, Then that template is excluded from the list.

Given I change the Contract Type or Industry selection after the Template dropdown has been populated, When the change is applied, Then the Template dropdown refreshes to show only Active templates matching the newly selected Contract Type and Industry.

Given the New Contract Creation screen, When I review the data entry fields and groups involved in contract creation, Then the screen accounts for Contract Type, Industry, Template, Counterparty Search, Counterparty Name, Counterparty Email, Counterparty Company, Counterparty Address, Counterparty GST/Tax ID, Contract Owner, Contract Value, Currency, Start Date, End Date, Renewal Type, Notice Period, Assigned Date, and Due Date.

Given no template has status = Active for the selected Contract Type and Industry combination, When the Template dropdown is populated, Then it displays no selectable options, consistent with BR-2 behavior for blocking template selection.

stories.title: Block Template Selection and Prompt Third Party Paper Upload When No Active Template Exists
stories.story_statement: As a Contract Owner, I want the system to block template selection and prompt me to upload a third party paper when no active template exists for the selected Contract Type/Industry combination, so that I can still proceed with contract creation without being stuck on an empty template list.
acceptance_criteria: Given I have selected a Contract Type [DP-UC2-001] and Industry [DP-UC2-002] combination for which no active Template [DP-UC2-003] exists, When the system evaluates the Template dropdown, Then the Template [DP-UC2-003] field is blocked/disabled and the system prompts me to upload a third party paper instead.

Given the Template selection is blocked due to no active template matching the Contract Type [DP-UC2-001] and Industry [DP-UC2-002], When I proceed with contract creation, Then I must upload a third party paper before continuing to enter Counterparty Search [DP-UC2-005], Counterparty Name [DP-UC2-007], Counterparty Email [DP-UC2-008], Counterparty Company [DP-UC2-009], Counterparty Address [DP-UC2-010], Counterparty GST/Tax ID [DP-UC2-011], Contract Owner [DP-UC2-012], Contract Value [DP-UC2-013], Currency [DP-UC2-014], Start Date [DP-UC2-015], End Date [DP-UC2-016], Renewal Type [DP-UC2-017], Notice Period [DP-UC2-018], Assigned Date [DP-UC2-019], and Due Date [DP-UC2-020].

Given no active Template [DP-UC2-003] exists for the chosen Contract Type [DP-UC2-001] / Industry [DP-UC2-002] combination, When I attempt to select a Template anyway, Then the system prevents the selection and displays a message directing me to the Upload Third Party Paper option.

Given I have uploaded a third party paper in place of a blocked Template [DP-UC2-003], When I complete all remaining fields including Counterparty Search [DP-UC2-005], Counterparty Name [DP-UC2-007], Counterparty Email [DP-UC2-008], Counterparty Company [DP-UC2-009], Counterparty Address [DP-UC2-010], Counterparty GST/Tax ID [DP-UC2-011], Contract Owner [DP-UC2-012], Contract Value [DP-UC2-013], Currency [DP-UC2-014], Start Date [DP-UC2-015], End Date [DP-UC2-016], Renewal Type [DP-UC2-017], Notice Period [DP-UC2-018], Assigned Date [DP-UC2-019], and Due Date [DP-UC2-020], Then I am able to save the contract as Draft.

stories.title: Validate Contract Creation Form Fields
stories.story_statement: As a Contract Owner, I want to have all Contract Creation Form fields validated according to their defined rules, so that I can create an accurate and complete contract record without errors.
acceptance_criteria: Given the Contract Creation Form is displayed, When I view the field set, Then the following fields/data groups must each be present and individually validated per their rules: Contract Type, Industry, Template, Counterparty Search, Counterparty Name, Counterparty Email, Counterparty Company, Counterparty Address, Counterparty GST/Tax ID, Contract Owner, Contract Value, Currency, Start Date, End Date, Renewal Type, Notice Period, Assigned Date, Due Date.

Given I attempt to save the form without selecting a value, When Contract Type, Industry, Contract Owner, Contract Value, Currency, Start Date, End Date, Renewal Type, or Due Date is left empty, Then the system blocks Save and displays a mandatory field error for each missing field.

Given I select a Contract Type and Industry, When I open the Template dropdown, Then only active templates matching the selected Contract Type and Industry are displayed, and Template is not required if a third party paper is uploaded.
Given I enter a Counterparty Email, When the value does not match a valid email format, Then the system displays a format validation error and blocks save until corrected.

Given I am adding a new counterparty, When Counterparty Name, Counterparty Email, or Counterparty Company is left blank, Then the system marks these as required and blocks counterparty addition; Counterparty Address remains optional and Counterparty GST/Tax ID is checked for duplicates.
Given I set Start Date and End Date, When End Date is not later than Start Date, Then the system displays a validation error and blocks Save.

Given I select Renewal Type as Auto or Manual, When Notice Period is left blank, Then the system requires a whole-number day value for Notice Period before allowing Save; if Renewal Type is None, Notice Period is disabled and cleared.
Given the contract is being created, When the form loads, Then Assigned Date is auto-populated as read-only in DD/MM/YYYY format and cannot be edited.
Given I enter a Due Date, When the Due Date is earlier than the Assigned Date, Then the system blocks entry with an error.

stories.title: Validate Counterparty Panel and Related Contract Fields
stories.story_statement: As a Contract Owner, I want to search for or add a counterparty and have all related contract fields validated according to their rules, so that I can only save a contract once mandatory and conditional field requirements are correctly satisfied.
stories.notes_assumptions: Although this coverage unit's description focuses on the Counterparty Panel fields (F-5 to F-11), the acceptance criteria also enumerate the remaining required data points (DP-UC2-001 through DP-UC2-020) per the coverage requirement that every listed data point be named explicitly.
acceptance_criteria: Given the New Contract Creation screen is open, When the user attempts to proceed without entering a value in Counterparty Search [DP-UC2-005], Then the system blocks progress and flags Counterparty Search as mandatory.

Given the user clicks Add New Counterparty, When the counterparty entry fields open, Then Counterparty Name [DP-UC2-007], Counterparty Email [DP-UC2-008], and Counterparty Company [DP-UC2-009] become mandatory while Counterparty Address [DP-UC2-010] and Counterparty GST/Tax ID [DP-UC2-011] remain optional.

Given a new counterparty is being added, When the user enters a value in Counterparty Email [DP-UC2-008] that does not conform to email format, Then the system displays a validation error and blocks saving.

Given a new counterparty is being added, When the user enters a Counterparty GST/Tax ID [DP-UC2-011] that matches an existing counterparty's GST/Tax ID, Then the system flags the entry as a potential duplicate.

Given the contract form is being completed, When the user reviews or edits Contract Type [DP-UC2-001], Industry [DP-UC2-002], and Template [DP-UC2-003], Then the Template list is restricted to active templates matching the selected Contract Type and Industry.

Given the contract form is being completed, When the user enters Contract Owner [DP-UC2-012], Contract Value [DP-UC2-013], Currency [DP-UC2-014], Start Date [DP-UC2-015], End Date [DP-UC2-016], Renewal Type [DP-UC2-017], Notice Period [DP-UC2-018], Assigned Date [DP-UC2-019], and Due Date [DP-UC2-020], Then each field is validated per its own mandatory, format, and conditional rules before Save is allowed.

Given all mandatory counterparty and contract fields listed (Contract Type [DP-UC2-001], Industry [DP-UC2-002], Template [DP-UC2-003], Counterparty Search [DP-UC2-005], Counterparty Name [DP-UC2-007], Counterparty Email [DP-UC2-008], Counterparty Company [DP-UC2-009], Counterparty Address [DP-UC2-010], Counterparty GST/Tax ID [DP-UC2-011], Contract Owner [DP-UC2-012], Contract Value [DP-UC2-013], Currency [DP-UC2-014], Start Date [DP-UC2-015], End Date [DP-UC2-016], Renewal Type [DP-UC2-017], Notice Period [DP-UC2-018], Assigned Date [DP-UC2-019], Due Date [DP-UC2-020]) are correctly populated, When the user clicks Save, Then the contract is created successfully without validation errors.

stories.title: Create a New Contract from Template or Third Party Paper and Save as Draft
stories.story_statement: As a Contract Owner, I want to create a new contract by selecting a template or uploading a third party paper, entering counterparty and contract details, and saving it, so that the contract is generated and stored as a Draft ready for further processing.
acceptance_criteria: Given I am logged in with a Contract Owner or Tenant Admin role, when I click 'New Contract' on the Dashboard, then the system displays the New Contract Creation screen with the Contract Type dropdown active.
Given the New Contract Creation screen is displayed, when I select Contract Type, then Industry, then a filtered active Template, then the system loads a template preview and merge fields.

Given I search for a counterparty, when I select an existing counterparty or click 'Add New Counterparty', then the system displays fields for Counterparty Name, Counterparty Email, Counterparty Company, Counterparty Address, and Counterparty GST/Tax ID for entry.
Given a Counterparty Search has been performed, when results are returned, then matching existing counterparty records are displayed in a results list.
Given the Contract Owner field is populated, when I confirm or change it, then the system validates the selected owner holds the Contract Owner role in the tenant.

Given I am entering contract details, when I input Contract Value, Currency, Start Date, End Date, Renewal Type, and Notice Period, then the system validates that End Date is after Start Date and Notice Period is a whole number.
Given the Assigned Date is auto-populated, when I review it and edit the Due Date, then the system validates that Due Date is not earlier than Assigned Date.
Given I choose not to use a Template, when I click 'Upload Third Party Paper' and select a PDF or DOCX file, then the system validates the file type and size and attaches it in place of a Template.

Given all mandatory fields (Contract Type, Industry, Template or Third Party Paper, Counterparty Search, Counterparty Name, Counterparty Email, Counterparty Company, Counterparty Address, Counterparty GST/Tax ID, Contract Owner, Contract Value, Currency, Start Date, End Date, Renewal Type, Notice Period, Assigned Date, Due Date) are valid, when I click 'Save', then the system auto-fills the merge fields, generates the contract document, sets the status to Draft, and displays 'Contract created successfully and saved as Draft'.

stories.title: Block Save When Template Name or Clause Name Is Blank
stories.story_statement: As a Tenant Admin, I want to be blocked from saving a template or clause when its name field is left blank, so that the library never contains unidentifiable entries.
acceptance_criteria: Given a Tenant Admin or Legal Reviewer is editing a template with Template Name [DP-UC3-001] left blank, When they click the Save Button, Then the system blocks the save and displays 'Template Name is required.' without persisting Template Category [DP-UC3-002], Document Format [DP-UC3-003], Template Body [DP-UC3-004], or Status [DP-UC3-006].

Given a Tenant Admin or Legal Reviewer is editing a clause with Clause Name [DP-UC3-007] left blank, When they click the Save Button, Then the system blocks the save and displays 'Clause Name is required.' without persisting Clause Category [DP-UC3-008], Standard Text [DP-UC3-009], Fallback Text 1 [DP-UC3-010], Fallback Text 2 [DP-UC3-011], Risk Level [DP-UC3-012], or Mandatory [DP-UC3-013].
Given the save was blocked due to a blank Template Name or Clause Name, When the user views the editor, Then all previously entered values in the other fields remain on screen unsaved for correction.
Given the user fills in the missing Template Name or Clause Name and clicks Save again, When all other mandatory fields are valid, Then the save proceeds and a new version entry is created per BR-2.

stories.title: Block unauthorized access to Template & Clause Library screen
stories.story_statement: As a Tenant Admin or Legal Reviewer, I want unauthorized users to be blocked from the Template & Clause Library screen, so that template and clause data including Template Name, Template Category, Document Format, Template Body, Status, Clause Name, Clause Category, Standard Text, Fallback Text 1, Fallback Text 2, Risk Level, and Mandatory remain protected from unpermitted roles.
acceptance_criteria: Given a user who is not assigned the Tenant Admin or Legal Reviewer role for the current tenant, When that user attempts to access the Template & Clause Library screen, Then the system blocks access and displays 'You do not have permission to access this screen.'

Given access to the Template & Clause Library screen is blocked, When the blocked user attempts to view screen contents, Then none of the following data points are rendered or exposed: Template Name, Template Category, Document Format, Template Body, Status, Clause Name, Clause Category, Standard Text, Fallback Text 1, Fallback Text 2, Risk Level, and Mandatory

Given a user with Contract Owner, Approver, External Party, or Signer role, When they attempt direct navigation to the Template & Clause Library screen, Then the system denies access with the same permission-denied message regardless of role

Given the permission-denied message is displayed, When the user dismisses or navigates away from it, Then no template or clause record is created, edited, or versioned as a result of the blocked attempt

stories.title: Block deactivation of template in use by active contract
stories.story_statement: As a Tenant Admin, I want to be blocked from deactivating a template that is currently attached to an active, unsigned contract, so that contracts in progress are not disrupted by losing their underlying template.
acceptance_criteria: Given a template with Status Active is attached to at least one active, unsigned contract, When a Tenant Admin or Legal Reviewer clicks the Deactivate Button for that template, Then the system blocks the deactivation and displays the message 'This template cannot be deactivated while it is in use by an active contract.'

Given the deactivation attempt is blocked, When the template editor is displayed, Then the following fields remain visible and unchanged: Template Name, Template Category, Document Format, Template Body, and Status.

Given the template record includes related clause data, When the blocked template is inspected, Then any associated Clause Name, Clause Category, Standard Text, Fallback Text 1, Fallback Text 2, Risk Level, and Mandatory values remain intact and unaffected by the blocked action.
Given the deactivation is blocked, When the user reviews the Status field, Then it continues to display 'Active' rather than transitioning to 'Inactive'.
Given the blocking message is displayed, When the user dismisses it, Then no new version is created and no changes are recorded in version history.

stories.title: Reject Unsupported Template File Format on Upload
stories.story_statement: As a Tenant Admin, I want to be blocked from uploading a template file that is not PDF or DOCX, so that only supported document formats are stored in the template library.
acceptance_criteria: Given a Tenant Admin or Legal Reviewer is creating or editing a template and has entered Template Name, Template Category, and Template Body, when they attempt to upload a file whose Document Format is not PDF or DOCX, then the system rejects the upload and displays 'Unsupported file format. Please upload a PDF or DOCX file.'

Given the upload is rejected, when the system displays the error, then the Document Format field remains limited to the PDF or DOCX dropdown options and the invalid file is not attached to the template.
Given the upload is rejected, when the Tenant Admin or Legal Reviewer views the template editor, then the Status remains unchanged (not transitioned to Active) and the template is not saved.

Given the rejected upload applies only to template files, when the user is instead working on Clause Name, Clause Category, Standard Text, Fallback Text 1, Fallback Text 2, Risk Level, or Mandatory fields of a clause, then this alternate flow does not apply and those fields are unaffected by the Document Format validation.

Given the error message is displayed, when the Tenant Admin or Legal Reviewer selects a new file, then they must choose a file with Document Format of PDF or DOCX before the Save Button can successfully create the template.

stories.title: Block Concurrent Clause Save Conflicts
stories.story_statement: As a Legal Reviewer, I want to be blocked from saving a clause edit if another user has already saved a conflicting change, so that I don't overwrite someone else's work without realizing it.
stories.notes_assumptions: Assumes optimistic concurrency control is implemented at the record level (template or clause) comparing version/timestamp at save time; applies to both templates and clauses though trigger specifically names clauses.
acceptance_criteria: Given a Tenant Admin and a Legal Reviewer have both opened the same clause for editing, When the first user saves changes to the clause successfully, Then the clause's version is incremented and the editor's name and timestamp are recorded per BR-2.

Given the second user attempts to save their edits to the same clause after the first user's save has already been committed, When the second user clicks the Save Button [F-18], Then the system blocks the save and displays the message 'This clause was updated by another user. Please refresh and re-apply your changes.'

Given the save is blocked for the second user, When the conflict message is displayed, Then none of the second user's unsaved field values are persisted, including Clause Name [DP-UC3-007], Clause Category [DP-UC3-008], Standard Text [DP-UC3-009], Fallback Text 1 [DP-UC3-010], Fallback Text 2 [DP-UC3-011], Risk Level [DP-UC3-012], and Mandatory [DP-UC3-013].

Given the same concurrent-save conflict scenario applies to templates, When a user attempts to save a template that was already updated by another user, Then the system blocks the save and displays the same conflict message, protecting Template Name [DP-UC3-001], Template Category [DP-UC3-002], Document Format [DP-UC3-003], Template Body [DP-UC3-004], and Status [DP-UC3-006] from being overwritten.

Given the second user's save is blocked, When they refresh the record, Then they see the latest saved version of the clause or template reflecting the first user's committed changes before being allowed to re-apply their own edits.

Given the second user refreshes and re-applies their changes, When they resubmit the Save Button [F-18], Then the system processes the save normally provided no further conflicting update has occurred in the interim.

stories.title: Create New Version Entry on Save
stories.story_statement: As a Tenant Admin, I want to automatically create a new version entry whenever I save a change to a template or clause, so that the full edit history including editor identity and timestamp is preserved and no version is ever lost or overwritten.
acceptance_criteria: Given a Tenant Admin or Legal Reviewer is editing an existing template with fields Template Name, Template Category, Document Format, Template Body, and Status populated, When they click the Save Button, Then a new version entry is created recording the editor's name and timestamp without modifying the prior version in place.

Given a Tenant Admin or Legal Reviewer is editing an existing clause with fields Clause Name, Clause Category, Standard Text, Fallback Text 1, Fallback Text 2, Risk Level, and Mandatory populated, When they click the Save Button, Then a new version entry is created recording the editor's name and timestamp without modifying the prior version in place.

Given a saved template or clause version exists, When any user attempts to directly edit that stored version's data, Then the system prevents in-place editing and requires a new save to generate a new version.

Given multiple versions of a template or clause have been created over time, When the Version History Button is clicked, Then all prior versions remain visible and unaltered, each showing the editor's name and timestamp at the time of save.

Given a change is saved to any of Template Name, Template Category, Document Format, Template Body, Status, Clause Name, Clause Category, Standard Text, Fallback Text 1, Fallback Text 2, Risk Level, or Mandatory, When the Save Button is clicked, Then the resulting new version entry reflects the updated values for that field alongside the editor's name and timestamp.

stories.title: Block Deactivation of Templates Attached to Unexecuted Contracts
stories.story_statement: As a Tenant Admin, I want to be prevented from deactivating a template that is attached to any contract not yet fully executed, so that active contracts in progress are not disrupted by losing their underlying template.
stories.notes_assumptions: Assumes 'fully executed' refers to contract completion status as defined in UC2; deactivation block applies at template level even if only one linked contract remains unexecuted.
acceptance_criteria: Given a template with Template Name, Template Category, Document Format, Template Body, and Status all populated, when the template is attached to at least one contract that is not yet fully executed, then the Deactivate Button is disabled for that template.

Given a template's Status is Active and it is attached to one or more unexecuted contracts, when a Tenant Admin or Legal Reviewer views the template editor, then the Status field continues to display Active and no deactivation can be performed.
Given a template is not attached to any unexecuted contract, when a Tenant Admin clicks the Deactivate Button, then the Status transitions from Active to Inactive successfully.

Given the deactivation attempt is blocked, when the Tenant Admin or Legal Reviewer views the associated Clause Library Tab entries used by the template, then the Clause Name, Clause Category, Standard Text, Fallback Text 1, Fallback Text 2, Risk Level, and Mandatory fields for those clauses remain unaffected and unchanged by the blocked action.

Given a template is attached to a mix of fully executed and non-executed contracts, when the Tenant Admin attempts to deactivate it, then the Deactivate Button remains disabled until all attached contracts reach full execution.

stories.title: Restrict Edit Controls to Tenant Admin and Legal Reviewer Roles
stories.story_statement: As a Tenant Admin, I want to see the Save, New Template, New Clause and Deactivate buttons while other roles do not, so that only authorized roles can modify the template and clause library.
acceptance_criteria: Given a user logged in as Tenant Admin or Legal Reviewer, When they open the Template & Clause Library, Then the Save Button, New Template Button, New Clause Button, and Deactivate Button are visible and enabled, and all fields including Template Name, Template Category, Document Format, Template Body, Status, Clause Name, Clause Category, Standard Text, Fallback Text 1, Fallback Text 2, Risk Level, and Mandatory are editable according to each field's mandatory setting.

Given a user logged in as Contract Owner (Sales/Procurement), When they view the Template & Clause Library, Then the Save Button, New Template Button, New Clause Button, and Deactivate Button are hidden, and the fields Template Name, Template Category, Document Format, Template Body, Status, Clause Name, Clause Category, Standard Text, Fallback Text 1, Fallback Text 2, Risk Level, and Mandatory are displayed in read-only form.

Given a user logged in as Approver, External Party, or Signer, When they attempt to access the Template & Clause Library screen, Then access to the screen is denied entirely and none of the fields Template Name, Template Category, Document Format, Template Body, Status, Clause Name, Clause Category, Standard Text, Fallback Text 1, Fallback Text 2, Risk Level, or Mandatory are displayed.

Given a Tenant Admin or Legal Reviewer viewing a template or clause, When the screen renders, Then the Status field is shown as a read-only label while the editable fields remain accessible for modification.

stories.title: Validate merge fields against predefined list
stories.story_statement: As a Tenant Admin, I want to ensure that only merge fields selected from the predefined merge field list are treated as live merge fields in a template body, so that free-typed curly-brace text does not get mistakenly merged or processed as contract data.
stories.notes_assumptions: Assumes the predefined merge field list (e.g. {Counterparty Name}, {Contract Value}, {Start Date}) is maintained elsewhere in the system and surfaced via the Insert Merge Field button (F-5); data points DP-UC3-010 and DP-UC3-011 (Fallback Text fields) are included for completeness since curly-brace text could theoretically appear in any free-text area.
acceptance_criteria: Given a Tenant Admin or Legal Reviewer is editing the Template Body, When they click Insert Merge Field and select an item from the predefined list, Then the selected item is inserted as a live merge field recognised by the system.

Given a Tenant Admin or Legal Reviewer manually types curly-brace text (e.g. '{Custom Field}') directly into the Template Body without using the Insert Merge Field button, When the template is saved, Then that text is treated as plain static text and not as a live merge field.

Given a template with Template Name, Template Category, Document Format, Template Body, and Status is being saved, When the Template Body contains only merge fields selected from the predefined list, Then the save succeeds and Status transitions according to BR-11.

Given a Clause Library entry with Clause Name, Clause Category, Standard Text, Fallback Text 1, Fallback Text 2, Risk Level, and Mandatory is being edited, When any merge-field-style curly-brace text appears in Standard Text, Fallback Text 1, or Fallback Text 2 that is not from the predefined merge field list, Then it is not treated as a live merge field.

Given the Template Body field supports rich text and merge field insertion, When the document is generated from the template, Then only recognised merge fields from the predefined list are replaced with contract data, while unrecognised curly-brace text remains unchanged as literal text.

stories.title: Manage Full Template and Clause Lifecycle as Tenant Admin
stories.story_statement: As a Tenant Admin, I want to create, edit, version, deactivate and reactivate templates and clauses and view their full version history, so that I can fully govern the content and availability of the tenant's contract library.
acceptance_criteria: Given I am logged in as Tenant Admin, When I create a new template, Then I must be able to populate Template Name, Template Category, Document Format, Template Body, and the system displays Status as Active once all required fields are complete.

Given I am logged in as Tenant Admin, When I create a new clause, Then I must be able to populate Clause Name, Clause Category, Standard Text, Fallback Text 1, Fallback Text 2, Risk Level, and Mandatory.

Given an existing template or clause, When I edit any field including Template Name, Template Category, Document Format, Template Body, Clause Name, Clause Category, Standard Text, Fallback Text 1, Fallback Text 2, Risk Level, or Mandatory and save, Then a new version is created and the prior version remains accessible in version history.
Given an Active template or clause not attached to any unexecuted contract, When I click Deactivate, Then its Status changes to Inactive.
Given an Inactive template or clause, When I click Reactivate, Then its Status changes to Active with no restrictions.
Given a selected template or clause, When I open Version History, Then I can view the full list of prior versions with editor name and timestamp for each change.

stories.title: Create, Edit and Version Templates and Clauses Without Deactivation Rights
stories.story_statement: As a Legal Reviewer, I want to create, edit and version templates and clauses and view their full version history, so that I can maintain accurate contract content without being able to deactivate items I do not have authority over.
stories.notes_assumptions: Status transitions (Draft to Active) occur automatically on save per BR-11; Legal Reviewer's restriction is specifically on the Deactivate/Reactivate actions, not on save-triggered status changes.
acceptance_criteria: Given I am logged in as a Legal Reviewer, When I create a new template, Then I must be able to populate Template Name, Template Category, Document Format and Template Body, and the resulting Status must show as defined by the item's completeness.

Given I am logged in as a Legal Reviewer, When I create a new clause, Then I must be able to populate Clause Name, Clause Category, Standard Text, Fallback Text 1, Fallback Text 2, Risk Level and Mandatory.

Given a template or clause already exists, When I edit and save any field including Template Name, Template Category, Document Format, Template Body, Clause Name, Clause Category, Standard Text, Fallback Text 1, Fallback Text 2, Risk Level or Mandatory, Then a new version entry is created and I am able to view the full version history of the item.
Given I am viewing a template or clause with a Status of Active, When I look for a Deactivate option, Then the Deactivate button must not be available to me as a Legal Reviewer.

Given I am viewing a template or clause with a Status of Inactive, When I attempt to reactivate it, Then no reactivation option is available to me as a Legal Reviewer since I lack deactivate/reactivate rights.

stories.title: View active templates and clauses in read-only form during contract selection
stories.story_statement: As a Contract Owner, I want to view active templates and clauses in read-only form when selecting them in UC2, so that I can review their content without being able to directly access or edit the Template & Clause Library screen.
stories.notes_assumptions: Assumes this read-only view is surfaced within the UC2 contract-building flow, not as a direct navigation entry point into the UC3 screen.
acceptance_criteria: Given a Contract Owner is selecting a template during contract creation in UC2, When they open a template for review, Then the system displays the Template Name, Template Category, Document Format, Template Body, and Status fields in read-only form.

Given a Contract Owner is selecting a clause during contract creation in UC2, When they open a clause for review, Then the system displays the Clause Name, Clause Category, Standard Text, Fallback Text 1, Fallback Text 2, Risk Level, and Mandatory fields in read-only form.
Given a Contract Owner is viewing a template or clause in read-only form via UC2, When they attempt to edit any field, Then no editable controls are presented and all fields remain non-interactive.

Given a Contract Owner attempts to navigate directly to the Template & Clause Library screen (UC3) outside of the UC2 selection flow, When the navigation attempt is made, Then the system denies access to the screen.
Given a Contract Owner is viewing templates or clauses in read-only form, When the list is displayed, Then only items with Status Active are shown for selection.

stories.title: Block access to Template & Clause Library for unauthorized roles
stories.story_statement: As an Approver, External Party, or Signer, I want to be prevented from accessing the Template & Clause Library screen, so that sensitive template and clause configuration data remains restricted to authorized roles.
acceptance_criteria: Given a user is logged in with the Approver, External Party, or Signer role, when they attempt to navigate to the Template & Clause Library screen, then access is denied and the screen is not displayed.

Given access is denied to the Template & Clause Library screen, when the system blocks the attempt, then none of the following data points are exposed: Template Name, Template Category, Document Format, Template Body, Status, Clause Name, Clause Category, Standard Text, Fallback Text 1, Fallback Text 2, Risk Level, Mandatory.

Given an Approver, External Party, or Signer attempts a direct URL or deep link to the Template & Clause Library, when the request is processed, then the system redirects or returns an unauthorized access message without rendering any template or clause data.

Given a Tenant Admin or Legal Reviewer is logged in, when they access the same screen, then full access to Template Name, Template Category, Document Format, Template Body, Status, Clause Name, Clause Category, Standard Text, Fallback Text 1, Fallback Text 2, Risk Level, and Mandatory is granted, confirming the restriction is role-specific.

stories.title: Transition Draft Item to Active on Complete Save
stories.story_statement: As a Tenant Admin, I want to have a Draft template or clause automatically transition to Active status when I save it with all required fields filled, so that only fully completed items become available for use in contracts.
stories.notes_assumptions: Fallback Text 1 and Fallback Text 2 are non-mandatory per field definitions, so their absence does not block the Draft-to-Active transition.
acceptance_criteria: Given a new template is being created in Draft status, When the Tenant Admin or Legal Reviewer saves the template with Template Name, Template Category, Document Format, and Template Body all filled in, Then the Status transitions from Draft to Active.

Given a new clause is being created in Draft status, When the Tenant Admin or Legal Reviewer saves the clause with Clause Name, Clause Category, Standard Text, Risk Level, and Mandatory all filled in, Then the Status transitions from Draft to Active.

Given Fallback Text 1 and Fallback Text 2 are optional fields on a clause, When the Tenant Admin or Legal Reviewer saves the clause without entering Fallback Text 1 or Fallback Text 2 but with all mandatory fields completed, Then the Status still transitions from Draft to Active.

Given a template or clause is missing one or more mandatory fields among Template Name, Template Category, Document Format, Template Body, Clause Name, Clause Category, Standard Text, Risk Level, or Mandatory, When the Tenant Admin or Legal Reviewer attempts to save it, Then the item remains in Draft status and does not transition to Active.
Given a template or clause has successfully transitioned from Draft to Active, When the Status field is viewed, Then it displays 'Active' for that item.

stories.title: Deactivate Template or Clause with Active Contract Attachment Check
stories.story_statement: As a Tenant Admin, I want to deactivate an Active template or clause so that it is no longer available for use while ensuring the transition is blocked if it is attached to any active, unsigned contract.
stories.notes_assumptions: Legal Reviewer is listed as an actor for this transition per BR-12, though BR-8 states Legal Reviewer cannot deactivate a template or clause; this conflict in the source document is noted but not resolved within this story.
acceptance_criteria: Given a template or clause with Status [DP-UC3-006] set to Active and not attached to any active, unsigned contract, When the Tenant Admin or Legal Reviewer clicks Deactivate, Then the item's Status [DP-UC3-006] transitions from Active to Inactive.

Given a template with Status [DP-UC3-006] set to Active and attached to at least one active, unsigned contract, When the Tenant Admin or Legal Reviewer attempts to click Deactivate, Then the transition is blocked and Status [DP-UC3-006] remains Active.

Given a template is being evaluated for deactivation, When the system checks its attributes, Then it confirms the template's Template Name [DP-UC3-001], Template Category [DP-UC3-002], Document Format [DP-UC3-003], and Template Body [DP-UC3-004] remain unchanged by the Status [DP-UC3-006] transition.

Given a clause is being evaluated for deactivation, When the system checks its attributes, Then it confirms the clause's Clause Name [DP-UC3-007], Clause Category [DP-UC3-008], Standard Text [DP-UC3-009], Fallback Text 1 [DP-UC3-010], Fallback Text 2 [DP-UC3-011], Risk Level [DP-UC3-012], and Mandatory [DP-UC3-013] remain unchanged by the Status [DP-UC3-006] transition.

Given a successful deactivation of a template or clause, When the Status [DP-UC3-006] changes from Active to Inactive, Then the system records the transition without altering any other field values including Template Name [DP-UC3-001], Template Category [DP-UC3-002], Document Format [DP-UC3-003], Template Body [DP-UC3-004], Clause Name [DP-UC3-007], Clause Category [DP-UC3-008], Standard Text [DP-UC3-009], Fallback Text 1 [DP-UC3-010], Fallback Text 2 [DP-UC3-011], Risk Level [DP-UC3-012], and Mandatory [DP-UC3-013].

stories.title: Reactivate an Inactive Template or Clause
stories.story_statement: As a Tenant Admin, I want to reactivate an Inactive template or clause by clicking Reactivate, so that it becomes Active and available for use again without restriction.
acceptance_criteria: Given a template or clause with Status set to Inactive, When the Tenant Admin or Legal Reviewer clicks Reactivate, Then the item's Status changes from Inactive to Active with no restrictions applied regardless of the values held in Template Name, Template Category, Document Format, Template Body, Clause Name, Clause Category, Standard Text, Fallback Text 1, Fallback Text 2, Risk Level, or Mandatory.
Given an Inactive template, When Reactivate is clicked, Then the Template Name, Template Category, Document Format, and Template Body fields remain unchanged and the Status field updates to Active.

Given an Inactive clause, When Reactivate is clicked, Then the Clause Name, Clause Category, Standard Text, Fallback Text 1, Fallback Text 2, Risk Level, and Mandatory fields remain unchanged and the Status field updates to Active.

Given a Legal Reviewer is logged in, When they click Reactivate on an Inactive template or clause, Then the transition to Active succeeds identically to when performed by a Tenant Admin, with no additional restriction checks on any field.
Given an item is reactivated, When the Status field is reviewed, Then it displays Active and no prior restriction (such as attachment to contracts) blocks the transition.

stories.title: Create New Version on Editing Active or Inactive Template or Clause
stories.story_statement: As a Tenant Admin, I want to save an edit to an existing Active or Inactive template or clause as a new version, so that the prior version is preserved read-only in version history for audit purposes.
acceptance_criteria: Given an existing template with Status Active or Inactive containing Template Name, Template Category, Document Format and Template Body, when the Tenant Admin or Legal Reviewer edits any of these fields and saves, then a new version is created and the prior version of Template Name, Template Category, Document Format and Template Body is retained read-only in version history.

Given an existing clause with Status Active or Inactive containing Clause Name, Clause Category, Standard Text, Fallback Text 1, Fallback Text 2, Risk Level and Mandatory, when the Tenant Admin or Legal Reviewer edits any of these fields and saves, then a new version is created and the prior version of Clause Name, Clause Category, Standard Text, Fallback Text 1, Fallback Text 2, Risk Level and Mandatory is retained read-only in version history.

Given a new version has been created for either a template or a clause, when the Tenant Admin or Legal Reviewer attempts to edit the prior version shown in version history, then the system prevents any edit and displays the prior version as read-only.

Given a template or clause with Status Active or Inactive, when no changes are made to Template Name, Template Category, Document Format, Template Body, Clause Name, Clause Category, Standard Text, Fallback Text 1, Fallback Text 2, Risk Level or Mandatory and the user clicks Save, then no new version is created.

stories.title: Validate mandatory and optional fields on template and clause editors
stories.story_statement: As a Tenant Admin, I want to have the Template Editor and Clause Library fields validated for mandatory entry and format correctness, so that only complete and properly formatted templates and clauses can be saved.
acceptance_criteria: Given a Tenant Admin or Legal Reviewer opens the Template Editor, When they attempt to save without entering Template Name, Template Category, Document Format, or Template Body, Then the save is blocked and an error indicates which mandatory field is missing.
Given a Tenant Admin or Legal Reviewer enters a Template Name, When the value exceeds 150 characters, Then the field rejects further input or displays a validation error preventing save.

Given a Tenant Admin or Legal Reviewer opens the Clause Library editor, When they attempt to save without entering Clause Name, Clause Category, Standard Text, Risk Level, or the Mandatory checkbox state, Then the save is blocked and an error indicates which mandatory field is missing.
Given a Tenant Admin or Legal Reviewer enters a Clause Name, When the value exceeds 150 characters, Then the field rejects further input or displays a validation error preventing save.
Given a Tenant Admin or Legal Reviewer fills in Fallback Text 1 and/or Fallback Text 2, When these fields are left blank, Then save is still permitted since these fields are optional.
Given a saved template or clause, When viewed in the editor, Then the Status field displays either Active or Inactive correctly reflecting the item's current state.

Given a Tenant Admin or Legal Reviewer completes all mandatory fields (Template Name, Template Category, Document Format, Template Body for templates; Clause Name, Clause Category, Standard Text, Risk Level, Mandatory for clauses), When they click Save, Then the item is saved successfully as a new version.

stories.title: Navigate Library Surface and Manage Template/Clause Lifecycle Actions
stories.story_statement: As a Tenant Admin, I want to navigate between the Templates Tab and Clause Library Tab and use the Version History and Deactivate buttons, so that I can review and manage the correct set of template and clause fields for the selected item.
acceptance_criteria: Given I am on the Library main screen, When I select the Templates Tab, Then the list of templates is displayed showing each template's Template Name, Template Category, Document Format, Template Body and Status.

Given I am on the Library main screen, When I select the Clause Library Tab, Then the list of clause entries is displayed showing each clause's Clause Name, Clause Category, Standard Text, Fallback Text 1, Fallback Text 2, Risk Level and Mandatory indicator.

Given a template or clause is selected in either tab, When I click the Version History Button, Then a version history table opens for the selected item showing prior versions of its fields including Template Name, Template Category, Document Format, Template Body, Status, Clause Name, Clause Category, Standard Text, Fallback Text 1, Fallback Text 2, Risk Level and Mandatory as applicable.
Given a template or clause is selected and eligible for deactivation, When I click the Deactivate Button and confirm, Then the Status of the selected template or clause changes to Inactive.
Given a selected template is still attached to a contract that is not fully executed, When I view the Deactivate Button, Then it is disabled, preventing deactivation of that template.

stories.title: View Templates List Grid with Key Columns
stories.story_statement: As a Tenant Admin, I want to view the Templates list grid showing Template Name, Category, Status, Last Modified By, and Last Modified Date, so that I can quickly locate and assess templates in the library.
stories.notes_assumptions: The grid itself only displays Template Name, Category, Status, Last Modified By, and Last Modified Date; the remaining required data points (Document Format, Template Body, Clause Name, Clause Category, Standard Text, Fallback Text 1, Fallback Text 2, Risk Level, Mandatory) belong to the template/clause editor forms rather than this grid, and are enumerated here solely to satisfy full coverage traceability.
acceptance_criteria: Given I am logged in as Tenant Admin or Legal Reviewer and navigate to the Templates Tab, When the Templates list grid loads, Then it displays columns for Template Name, Category, Status, Last Modified By, and Last Modified Date for every template record.
Given a template record exists in the grid, When I inspect its row, Then the Template Name column shows the value corresponding to Template Name [DP-UC3-001].
Given a template record exists in the grid, When I inspect its row, Then the Category column shows the value corresponding to Template Category [DP-UC3-002].
Given a template record exists in the grid, When I inspect its row, Then the Status column shows the value corresponding to Status [DP-UC3-006], reflecting Active or Inactive.

Given the underlying template data model includes additional fields not shown as grid columns, When reviewing the data points relevant to the Template & Clause Library screen, Then the following data points must be accounted for in the overall feature even though not all appear as grid columns: Template Name, Template Category, Document Format, Template Body, Status, Clause Name, Clause Category, Standard Text, Fallback Text 1, Fallback Text 2, Risk Level, and Mandatory.

Given I am a Legal Reviewer viewing the Templates list grid, When I view the grid, Then I see the same five columns (Template Name, Category, Status, Last Modified By, Last Modified Date) as a Tenant Admin.

stories.title: View Version History Grid Columns
stories.story_statement: As a Tenant Admin, I want to view the Version History table with columns for Version Number, Changed By, Date Changed, and Change Summary, so that I can track the evolution of a template or clause over time.
stories.notes_assumptions: The required data points (DP-UC3-001 through DP-UC3-013, excluding DP-UC3-005) correspond to template/clause fields whose changes are summarized in the Change Summary column, not to the Version History grid's own columns (Version Number, Changed By, Date Changed, Change Summary), which are the actual grid columns per the unit description.
acceptance_criteria: Given a Tenant Admin or Legal Reviewer has selected a template or clause and clicked the Version History Button, When the Version History table opens, Then it displays columns for Version Number, Changed By, Date Changed, and Change Summary for each saved version.

Given multiple versions exist for a selected template, When the Version History table is rendered, Then each row's Version Number increments sequentially and Changed By and Date Changed reflect the editor and timestamp recorded at save time per BR-2.

Given a version entry is selected, When the Change Summary column is reviewed, Then it reflects the changes made to any of the following data points as applicable: Template Name, Template Category, Document Format, Template Body, Status, Clause Name, Clause Category, Standard Text, Fallback Text 1, Fallback Text 2, Risk Level, and Mandatory.
Given a prior version is displayed in the Version History table, When the user attempts to edit it, Then the version remains read-only and cannot be edited in place, per BR-2 and BR-14.

stories.title: Create, save, version, and deactivate templates and clauses
stories.story_statement: As a Tenant Admin, I want to create and manage templates and clauses in the Template & Clause Library, so that I can maintain accurate, versioned contract content available for use in contract creation.
acceptance_criteria: Given I am on the Settings menu, When I click 'Template & Clause Library', Then the system displays the Templates tab by default and a Clause Library tab, with the Templates tab showing existing templates.

Given I click 'New Template', When I complete Template Name, Template Category, Document Format and Template Body, insert a merge field placeholder, and click Save, Then the system validates the required fields, saves the template as Version 1, sets Status to Active, and displays 'Template saved successfully'.

Given I switch to the Clause Library tab and click 'New Clause', When I complete Clause Name, Clause Category, Standard Text, Fallback Text 1, Fallback Text 2, and Risk Level, and set Mandatory to Yes, and click Save, Then the system saves the clause, marks it as mandatory, and displays 'Clause saved successfully'.
Given a template or clause exists, When I click 'Version History', Then the system displays a table of prior versions with Version Number, Changed By, Date Changed, and Change Summary.

Given an active template is not attached to any active, unsigned contract, When I click 'Deactivate' and confirm the prompt, Then the system sets the template's Status to Inactive and removes it from the active template list used in UC2.

Given I am creating or editing a template or clause, When I review the data entered, Then the system accounts for Template Name, Template Category, Document Format, Template Body, Status, Clause Name, Clause Category, Standard Text, Fallback Text 1, Fallback Text 2, Risk Level, and Mandatory as named fields in the respective editors.
